substitutesInfo.description: Replacement parts for this one: manufacturer-named successors and second sources. An entry with type 'successor' means THIS part is superseded by the named one, one hop, as the manufacturer states it - never inferred from a status of obsolete or from part-number similarity. The schema cannot check that the named part exists in the catalogue, or exists exactly once; that is the referential pass's job, as for CIAS component URIs. Evidence for the claim goes in the record's provenance[] with fields: ["substitutesInfo"], carrying the same sourceUrl, retrievedDate and verification stamp as any datasheet field.

datasheetInfo.title: capacitorDatasheetInfo
datasheetInfo.description: Information extracted from the component datasheet and PMs Excel data

factors.description: Derating factors for frequency and temperature

application.description: Manufacturer's recommended application / quality-grade categories, comma-joined as printed in the catalogue (e.g. Taiyo Yuden's grade taxonomy: 'Auto. (Powertrain/Safety)', 'Auto. (Body/Info) & High Reliability', 'Telecom-Infrastructure & Industrial', 'Medical (International Class. Ⅲ）', 'Medical (International Class. I ・ II)', 'General Equipment', 'Mobile Devices'). Free-form string — taxonomies are manufacturer-specific.

allOf.title: class2HasNoLinearTemperatureCoefficient
allOf.description: A Class-2 ceramic dielectric has no linear temperature coefficient to state (IEC 60384-9: its permittivity vs temperature is non-linear, so the standard bounds a total percent change instead). `thermal.temperatureCoefficient` is therefore forbidden on ceramic-class-2 parts; use `thermal.capacitanceChangeOverTemperature`.

dielectricCode.description: Standard EIA / MIL dielectric code (e.g. X7R, X5R, C0G, NP0, Y5V, Y5U). Applies to ceramic technologies only; null or absent for non-ceramic chemistries.

qualifiedReliability.description: Failure-rate level this part is qualified to, for MIL-PRF-39003 / 39006 / 39014 and QPL parts. Part IDENTITY, beside `safetyClass` and `dielectricCode` rather than under `electrical`: the specification prints ONE ratings row covering every level, so the members of a rating differ ONLY by this and by their dash number. Without it, 4,878 of 6,373 MIL rows in the catalogue are byte-identical apart from a part number.

safetyClass.description: Interference-suppression safety class of the part (IEC 60384-14 / EN 60384-14 and their UL/CSA equivalents). This is part IDENTITY — a certification held by the series, like a dielectric code, not an electrical quantity — so it lives here beside `technology` and `dielectricCode` rather than under `electrical`. It states what the datasheet or the certificate says and NOTHING ELSE: a class is never to be inferred from rated voltage, technology, application text or a part-number substring. Null or absent means the class is unknown / not stated; the explicit class value `none` means the datasheet positively states the part carries no safety-class approval.

class.description: The safety class as certified. `x1`/`x2` are across-the-line (X) capacitors (IEC 60384-14 sub-class X1: peak impulse > 2.5 kV up to 4 kV; X2: <= 2.5 kV). `y1`/`y2`/`y4` are line-to-earth (Y) capacitors (Y1 double/reinforced insulation, 8 kV impulse; Y2 basic/supplementary, 5 kV; Y4 basic/supplementary, rated below 150 V, 2.5 kV). `x1y2` and `x1y1` are single values on purpose, not tidiness: dual-approved parts are real and their datasheets say so — Würth's WCAP-FTY2 marking block prints both "Safety Class & Rated Voltage: Y2, 300V~" and "X1, 330V~", and KEMET's R41 sheet is titled "Class X1/Y2" — and a single-valued enum would force a false answer on them. When `ratings` is present, `class` is the summary token for the same fact and must agree with it: a one-entry `ratings` uses that class's own token, a two-entry `ratings` uses the combined token. `none` means the sheet states no safety-class approval.

ratings.description: The certification stated per class. IEC 60384-14 grants a class AT a rated voltage, and a dual-approved part carries a DIFFERENT voltage for each class — TDK prints `X1/440VAC, Y1/400VAC` on one line, KEMET names `X1-440 Y2-300` in the series itself. One entry per class held, each with the AC voltage that class is granted at. Items use single-class tokens only: a rating belongs to one class by construction. Y-class voltages are bounded by the standard's own bands; X-class voltages are NOT, because IEC 60384-14 defines X sub-classes by peak impulse withstand, not by rated voltage. Omit when the datasheet states a class but no per-class voltage. Repeating a class to describe an assembly of several capacitors is not what this field is for — that is a CIAS brick of several capacitor parts.

class.description: The single class this rating is granted for.

ratedVoltageAc.description: Rated AC voltage in Volts RMS for THIS class, at the datasheet's reference frequency (50/60 Hz unless the sheet says otherwise).

standard.description: The standard this class is granted under, verbatim as printed, when it differs per class. Omit when the part-level `standard` covers both.
The safety standard the class is granted under, verbatim as the datasheet prints it (e.g. "IEC 60384-14", "EN 60384-14", "UL 60384-14"). Null or absent when the sheet names a class but no standard.

approvals.description: Approval identifiers held by the part or its series, as printed (e.g. "ENEC-02986", "UL E345659", "CSA E60384-14"). These are the certificate references that make the class a certification rather than a label. Null or absent when the sheet publishes none; an empty array means the same and is equally acceptable.

capacitanceMinimumLongTerm.description: Worst case of minimum capacitance (taking into account the tolerance) after end-of-life in Farads

capacitanceBiasPoints.description: Capacitance vs. DC-bias-voltage points (DC-bias derating curve, dominant for class-2 ceramics), each measured at a temperature and AC measurement voltage. voltage = DC bias in V, capacitance = effective capacitance in F at that bias.

capacitance.description: Effective capacitance at this DC bias in Farads.

ratedVoltage.description: Rated voltage in Volts. Required unless `voltageRatedAcMax` states a numeric AC rating: an AC-only interference-suppression (X/Y class) capacitor publishes no DC rating, and its AC figure belongs in `voltageRatedAcMax`, which is a DIFFERENT quantity. At least one of the two must be present; both may be.

polarized.description: True for polarized capacitors (aluminum electrolytic, tantalum, tantalum-polymer, niobium-oxide, supercapacitor-EDLC) that must see voltage of one fixed polarity only. False for ceramic, film, mica and other symmetric chemistries. Null when the librarian could not determine polarity from the datasheet — downstream selection logic should treat null as 'unknown, do not allow AC swing' (conservative).

voltageRatedDcMax.description: Maximum DC rated voltage in Volts

voltageRatedAcMax.description: Maximum continuous AC rated voltage in Volts RMS, at the datasheet's reference frequency (50/60 Hz unless the sheet says otherwise). This is the headline rating of an interference-suppression (X/Y class) capacitor — 275 / 300 / 305 / 310 / 440 V~ — and is a DIFFERENT quantity from `ratedVoltage` / `voltageRatedDcMax`, which are DC. Populate it only where the source publishes an AC rating; null or absent for DC-only parts.

dissipationFactorFrequency.description: Frequency at which the single-point dissipationFactor field above is measured, in Hz. Prefer dissipationFactorPoints for selection logic; this scalar pair is kept only for legacy datasheet values where no curve is available.

dissipationFactorPoints.description: Dissipation-factor-vs-frequency curve. xData = frequency in Hz, yData = tan delta as fraction (e.g. 0.025 for 2.5%). Same frequency-dependence motivation as esrPoints — DF and ESR are linked through DF = ESR * omega * C, so any chemistry whose ESR rises sharply at low frequency also shows a corresponding rise in DF. Selection logic must prefer this curve over the scalar dissipationFactor field when present.

qFactor.description: Quality factor (dimensionless, Q = 1/tan delta) as specified on the datasheet — for class-1 (C0G/NP0) MLCCs this is the specified MINIMUM Q at the standard measurement condition (EIA-198 / IEC 60384: Q ≥ 1000 for C ≥ 30 pF, Q ≥ 400 + 20·C[pF] below 30 pF, measured at 1 MHz, 1 Vrms). Q is strongly frequency-dependent, so pair this scalar with qFactorFrequency when the measurement frequency is known; absent qFactorFrequency means 'datasheet minimum at the manufacturer's standard condition', not a broadband value.

qFactorFrequency.description: Frequency at which the qFactor field above is specified, in Hz. Null or absent when the datasheet states only the standard-condition minimum without an explicit frequency.

esrFrequency.description: Frequency at which the single-point esr field above is measured, in Hz. Prefer esrPoints for selection logic; this scalar pair is kept only for legacy datasheet values where no curve is available.

impedancePoints.description: Impedance-magnitude-vs-frequency curve. xData = frequency in Hz, yData = |Z| in Ohms. The curve a designer actually reads for a decoupling or filtering part: it shows the capacitive region, the self-resonant minimum where |Z| bottoms out, and the inductive region above it — none of which the scalar capacitance and esr fields can express. MAS already carries impedancePoints for magnetics; this is the capacitor-side equivalent, same shape.

capacitanceFrequencyPoints.description: Effective-capacitance-vs-frequency curve. xData = frequency in Hz, yData = capacitance in Farads. Distinct from capacitanceBiasPoints, which derates against DC bias: this one derates against frequency. Both effects are real and independent, and a class-2 ceramic loses capacitance to each of them separately.

inductanceFrequencyPoints.description: Equivalent-series-inductance (ESL) vs frequency. xData = frequency in Hz, yData = inductance in Henries. ESL governs behaviour ABOVE self-resonance, where the part stops acting as a capacitor and its impedance rises with frequency — which is what decides whether a decoupling capacitor works at the frequency it was chosen for. Legitimately absent for parts that never reach self-resonance inside the measured sweep; that is a real answer, not a gap.

rippleCurrentPoints.description: ABSOLUTE ripple-current capability vs frequency. xData = frequency in Hz, yData = current in AMPERES. Deliberately separate from rippleCurrentFrequencyPoints, which is a dimensionless 0-1 DERATING MULTIPLIER: vendors publish both shapes and they are not interchangeable, so amperes must never be written into the multiplier field (nothing downstream can detect that substitution). Prefer a vendor-published measured curve. Where the figures come from a vendor simulator sampled as if measured — K-SIM's self-heating model, for instance, whose delta-T convention is not stated — the provenance entry must say so, because a modelled 3.7 A and a datasheet 2.8 A for the same part are different claims.

esrPoints.description: ESR-vs-frequency curve. xData = frequency in Hz, yData = ESR in Ohms. Captures the strong frequency dependence of ESR for class-2 ceramic and polymer chemistries — at low frequency (sub-kHz, e.g. 50/60 Hz mains) ESR can be one to two orders of magnitude larger than its 100 kHz datasheet value (see https://passive-components.eu/esr-of-capacitors-mechanisms-measurements-and-impact-to-applications/ Fig. 4). Selection logic must prefer this curve over the scalar esr field when present.

rippleCurrentFrequency.description: Frequency at which ripple current is specified in Hz

rippleCurrentTemperature.description: Temperature at which ripple current is specified in °C

rippleCurrentFrequencyPoints.description: Ripple current derating curve as a function of frequency

rippleCurrentTemperaturePoints.description: Ripple current derating curve as a function of temperature

_esrWarning.description: Internal flag or message: ESR value estimated or extrapolated (not from datasheet). True/false flag or descriptive warning string.

anyOf.description: A part with a DC (or unqualified) rating states it in `ratedVoltage`, exactly as before.

An AC-only interference-suppression capacitor publishes no DC rating, so `ratedVoltage` may be omitted provided the AC rating is actually stated — `voltageRatedAcMax` must be present AND a number, since null means 'no AC rating published' and would otherwise leave the part with no rated voltage at all.

thermal.title: capacitorThermal
thermal.description: Thermal characteristics — extends PEAS datasheetInfoThermal with capacitance-temperature coefficient.

temperature.description: Operating temperature range of the part, in degrees Celsius. Optional; omit when the datasheet does not state it.

tcc.description: DEPRECATED (2026-09-05, ABT #544) — do not write this field on new records; read `temperatureCoefficient` (Class 1) or `capacitanceChangeOverTemperature` (Class 2) instead. It is kept, and still accepted, only so consumers written against it do not break. The defect: a single field was asked to hold two DIFFERENT physical quantities — EIA-198 / IEC 60384-8 gives Class-1 dielectrics a linear temperature COEFFICIENT in ppm/°C (a rate), while IEC 60384-9 gives Class-2 dielectrics a bounded total percent capacitance CHANGE over a stated temperature range (no rate exists; their permittivity vs temperature is non-linear). No unit could make one field hold both and stay sortable or comparable, so the field was split.

temperatureCoefficient.description: Class-1 (temperature-compensating) LINEAR TEMPERATURE COEFFICIENT of capacitance, in ppm/°C (equivalently ppm/K — the quantity is a rate, dC/C per kelvin, unit K^-1). This is the EIA-198 / IEC 60384-8 quantity named by the dielectric code: C0G/NP0 is 0 ± 30 ppm/°C, U2J is -750 ppm/°C (tolerance ±120). Store the RAW ppm number (-750, not -750e-6, not -0.075); `minimum`/`maximum` carry the tolerance band. Class-2 dielectrics have no such coefficient — use `capacitanceChangeOverTemperature` for those. Replaces `tcc` for Class-1 parts.

capacitanceChangeOverTemperature.description: Bounded TOTAL capacitance change over a stated temperature range, in percent — the EIA-198 / IEC 60384-9 Class-2 quantity (X7R: ±15 % over -55..+125 °C; X5R: ±15 % over -55..+85 °C; X7T: +22/-33 %). It is NOT a rate and is meaningless without the span it applies over, which is why `temperatureRange` is required beside `changePercent`. Class-1 and film parts may also carry it (a ppm/°C coefficient implies a total change once a ΔT is chosen), but a Class-1 part's primary figure is `temperatureCoefficient`. Replaces `tcc` for Class-2 parts.

changePercent.description: Capacitance change in PERCENT of the 25 °C value, as the datasheet prints it (X7R: minimum -15, maximum 15). Percent, not a fraction — the unit is in the field name so it cannot be misread; a `nominal` may be given when the datasheet states a typical, and omitted when the figure is only a bound.

temperatureRange.description: The temperature span, in degrees Celsius, over which `changePercent` is bounded (X7R: minimum -55, maximum 125). This is the range the percent figure is specified over and may be narrower than the part's full operating range in `temperature`.

minimum.description: Low end of the span, in degrees Celsius.

maximum.description: High end of the span, in degrees Celsius.

mechanical.title: capacitorMechanical
mechanical.description: Mechanical dimensions and shape information. NOTE: the scalar `footprint` field elsewhere in this schema is a mounting AREA in m^2 and is a different concept from `landPattern` (the pad/hole pattern) — the two deliberately carry different names.

pinout.description: Per-terminal function map (shared PEAS type, hoisted 2026-08). Real for polarized parts (anode/cathode) and multi-terminal parts (feedthrough, X2Y, 4-terminal low-ESL).

landPattern.description: Manufacturer-recommended PCB land pattern (shared PEAS type, hoisted 2026-08): pad centres, copper sizes and drills as the datasheet's recommended-layout drawing publishes them.

thickness.description: Thickness / T dimension in meters. Chip-style (MLCC) datasheets specify the body as L × W × T, where T is the dimension perpendicular to the mounting plane; unlike the EIA case code (which fixes only L × W), T varies per part with layer count. Kept separate from height to stay faithful to datasheet nomenclature.

footprint.description: PCB footprint area in square meters

lifetime.title: capacitorLifetime
lifetime.description: Reliability and lifetime parameters — extends PEAS datasheetInfoLifetime with capacitor-specific end-of-life definitions.

modelParams.title: capacitorModelParams
modelParams.description: Circuit model parameters for SPICE simulation

factors.title: capacitorFactors
factors.description: Derating factors as functions of frequency and temperature

rippleCurrentFrequencyFactorFrequency.description: Frequency values for ripple current derating curve

rippleCurrentTemperatureFactorTemperatur.description: Temperature values for ripple current derating curve

technology.title: technology
technology.description: Capacitor technology / chemistry family. Closed enum so downstream selection logic can dispatch on chemistry without parsing free-form strings. Ceramic class is the dielectric-temperature behaviour family (class-1 = temperature-stable C0G/NP0; class-2 = X7R/X5R/Y5V high-K, voltage- and temperature-dependent; class-3 = Y5U etc.). The standard EIA/MIL dielectric code (e.g. X7R, C0G) goes in dielectricCode. thin-film-silicon is deposited SiO2/SiON dielectric on a substrate (Kyocera AVX Accu-P, Murata silicon capacitors, Vishay RFCS) - a distinct technology from sintered ceramics (different dielectric and process; distributors list it as its own category) and from the polymer film-* values. film-acrylic is the polymer-multi-layer (PML) construction: a vapour-deposited cross-linked acrylate (acrylic resin) dielectric stacked in 1000-5000 sub-micron layers (e.g. Rubycon PMLCAP) - distinct from wound/stacked thermoplastic metallized film (polypropylene/polyester/PPS) in both dielectric and process.
